newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah soft amid ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah soft amid ample liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was soft against the dollar in morning trading on Friday as the market tone was seen slightly biddish on the dollar, dealers said.
They said the market was still edgy with on-going volatility in the region and rates could easily break through stop-loss limits which might spur another wave of covering.
"The market is still looking for some kind of equilibrium," one local bank dealer said.
"There is no clear trend yet. The feeling is that people dare not go short on dollars at present," the dealer said.
He said operators appeared to stay squared or slightly long on dollars due to ample rupiah in the money market.
"With the ample rupiah condition, it's not adviseable to be short on dollars," the dealer said, adding that going too long on dollars was also risky in the wake of current instability.
He said the rupiah could also stage a strong recovery because players did not know where the equilibrium should be.
One U.S. bank dealer said spot rates were expected to range between 2,470 and 2,480 on Friday. Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,478.0/80.0 at 0300 GMT against an opening of 2,472/75.

Dealers said the early high for the rupiah was 2,467. They said the rupiah was quoted at 2,485 and 2,490 in New York after the rupiah tumbled late on Wednesday on stop-loss dollar buying and short-covering after several stop-loss limits were broken.
The market was closed on Thursday for a public holiday.
The U.S. bank dealer said instability in the rupiah was mainly due to spillover from offshore attacks to the ringgit.
"The rupiah is not the main target. I don't know whether speculators would switch to Indonesia. If yes, the storm would then be stronger," she said.

Some dealers said the currency attack was not linked to Indonesia's sound fundamentals as it received on Thursday fresh loans of $5.3 billion from members of the Consultative Group for Indonesia (CGI), a donor group for Indonesia.
They said the figure was 0.7 percent higher than the previous year, suggesting sustained confidence in the Indonesian economy.
"The CGI should be good news, but instead you get speculators casting for victims in the region, including the rupiah," one said.
Dealers said liquidity was ample, with overnight rupiah traded at 12.0 percent in mid-morning. Overnight swap was at 0.3/0.5 and tom/next at 0.12/0.15 points.
One-month swap was at 17.0/19.0, two at 32.0/38.0, three at 51.0/54.0 and six at 103.0/106.0 points.
The U.S. bank dealer said swap rates were seen going with the trend in the spot market which was slightly biddish.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,377/2,681 and the conversion band to 2,437/2,485 on Wednesday.
